factProposals.value: Versioned workflows per work type: named steps, the steps each may move to, and one final step that completes the work order. Administrators publish and retire them; crews move work orders along them.

The existing behaviour is the built-in Standard workflow (Open, then Completed), used by every work type without its own. Work orders saved before workflows existed were put on Standard at the matching step.
factProposals.evidence: server/db.js (wf-standard-1, addWorkflowColumns); tests/workflows.test.js (saved before workflows existed)

factProposals.value: Each work order records its workflow version, current step and when it reached that step; status stays open or completed, so the Madison AI feed, public site and heat maps are unchanged.
factProposals.evidence: server/db.js (work_orders.workflow_id, current_step, step_entered_at); tests/workflowsHttp.test.js (published work order format is unchanged)

factProposals.value: Workflow administrators use an API client with the workflows:admin scope; crews and outside systems move work orders with work_orders:write. Neither scope grants the other.
Every workflow publish and retire, and every move of a work order between steps, is in the audit trail with the user (as user via system), time, and before and after values.
The city's real workflows per work type, and who may move a work order past each step, are not known; the pothole workflow in the tests and demo is made up.

decisions.statement: Model today's behaviour as a built-in Standard workflow that applies to every work type without its own.
decisions.rationale: Existing work keeps working exactly as before, with no migration choices for staff to make.

decisions.statement: Publish workflow changes as new versions and keep work orders on the version they started with.
decisions.rationale: A change can never leave a work order on a step that no longer exists.
decisions.evidence: server/workflows.js (publishWorkflow); tests/workflows.test.js (stays on its workflow version)

decisions.statement: Refuse any workflow where some work order could never be completed, listing every problem.
decisions.rationale: Work orders must always be able to finish; one complete list is easier to fix than one problem at a time.

decisions.statement: Keep the final step reachable only by completion, which needs a note.
decisions.rationale: Keeps the existing rule that no work order is closed without saying what was done.

decisions.statement: Show step changes on the public site only as "Progress update".
decisions.rationale: Step names are written by administrators and may be internal.
decisions.evidence: server/publicRequests.js (HISTORY_LABELS); tests/workflowsHttp.test.js (public sees a step change)

limitations.statement: Per-step role limits are stored but not enforced; any key with work_orders:write can make any allowed move.
There is no draft stage or administrator page; workflows are published directly through the API.
Refused workflow definitions are in the request log, not the audit trail, because nothing changed.
Workflow steps are not sent to GIS; GIS still receives only the status.
